The retail selling price charged to final consumers in department stores

The production volume where total revenue equals total cost, resulting in zero profit and zero loss
The price threshold where consumer demand drops to zero units due to consumer resistance

The selling price per unit minus the variable cost per unit (P - V)
The sum of total revenue and total factory depreciation expense
The retail price multiplied by the number of units returned by customers

subject: Business Analytics

question: If a company has Fixed Costs F = $120,000, Unit Variable Cost V = $30, and Selling Price P = $70, what is the break-even volume in units?

3,000 units
4,000 units
1,200 units

subject: Business Analytics
lecture_title: المحاضرة الثانية (Lecture 2 - Ch 2): Decision Models, Break-Even & Optimization
question: A firm has Fixed Costs F = $60,000, Selling Price P = $50, and Unit Variable Cost V = $20. If unit variable cost rises to $30 while fixed costs and selling price remain unchanged, what is the change in the break-even quantity?
options: The break-even quantity decreases from 3,000 units to 2,000 units
The break-even quantity remains completely unchanged at 2,000 units
The break-even quantity increases from 2,000 units to 3,000 units
The break-even quantity increases from 1,200 units to 2,000 units
explanation: Initially, Q_BE = $60,000 / ($50 - $20) = $60,000 / $30 = 2,000 units. When unit variable cost rises to $30, unit contribution drops to $20, increasing Q_BE to $60,000 / $20 = 3,000 units.

Neither model can be used to calculate price elasticity under any circumstances

When the objective function is strictly linear and has fewer than three decision variables
